Sect: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}

A practical clan with no known Antediluvian founder, the Panders are made up of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.SNuXttNqxzJ6uPXv]{Caitiff} childer Embraced into the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}, who have banded together as a clan of their own rather than remain without one. Young, rowdy, and eager to prove themselves, they have little use for pretensions of clan superiority.

Disciplines: Panders have no specific clan Disciplines; they choose and learn Disciplines as @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.SNuXttNqxzJ6uPXv]{Caitiff} do, drawing from any available source.

Organization: Panders rarely form their own packs of significance, more often filling out the ranks of mixed-clan packs and proving themselves through deeds rather than pedigree.

See also: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{the Sabbat} - the antitribu designation itself marks this bloodline's members as having sided with the Sabbat rather than the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}.

Advantage: The clanless Caitiff have no fixed clan Disciplines: they may develop any three Disciplines as their own.

Disadvantage: With no clan, a Caitiff has no clan weakness — but also no clan Disciplines by right, no elders or mentors, and little standing in Kindred society (and Caitiff are typically of higher generation).
